result:
I’d make uncertainty socially safe.

People could say **“I don’t know”** without being dismissed, **“I was wrong”** without being humiliated, and **“I’ve changed”** without being treated as a traitor. Not because conviction is bad, but because the fear of losing dignity keeps people defending beliefs, loyalties, and cruelties they might otherwise outgrow.

I suspect much of the world is held in place not by people being certain, but by people being terrified to admit they no longer are.
